mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weeks (-1.6 to -0.4 to -0.1 to 0.3), indicating positive momentum in discretionary mobility that is likely to persist via habit formation and continued loosening of movement patterns, producing a higher mean over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose monotonically from -1.6 to 0.3 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28 days despite the prior three-week monotonic increase.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility sustains above 4.5 percent for two consecutive weeks, it signals a durable return of office-based commuting, which generates incidental weekday retail and dining visits near workplaces, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean exceeds 4.5 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached 4.7 at t-2w before settling near 4.3-4.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of WORKPLACES crossing and holding above 4.5 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in PARKS mobility above -7 percent for two consecutive weeks reflects reduced public caution about outdoor and public gatherings, a behavioral shift that typically precedes renewed comfort with indoor retail and recreation visits, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -7 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -10.6 to -6.7 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stagnates or falls in the two weeks following PARKS crossing and holding above -7 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise in the same week, the combined effect of more commuters moving through transit hubs and more people at workplaces compounds to generate additional incidental retail stops, producing a larger RETAIL_REC increase than either series moving alone would predict, over a four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -0.1 to 0.7 while WORKPLACES rose from 3.9 to 4.7 between t-3w and t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks is no larger when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT co-rise than when only one rises, falsifying the interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility (above 40 percent) alongside flat RETAIL_REC growth indicates households are still prioritizing essential precautionary trips over discretionary retail outings, a cautious consumption pattern that will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 40 while RETAIL_REC fails to accelerate beyond its recent weekly increments
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed between 42.9 and 44.4 across all four weeks while RETAIL_REC rose only marginally
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially over the next four weeks even while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated above 40.

mechanism_narrative: Entering the year-end holiday shopping season in Singapore typically boosts retail and recreation footfall, but this seasonal lift will only materialize if RESIDENTIAL mobility stays below 5.0, confirming no renewed stay-home restrictions are suppressing movement; under that condition RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays below 5.0 through the next four weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has held steady between 3.7 and 4.0 for four weeks
fact:decision date 2021-11-15 is approaching the year-end holiday season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining below 5.0 throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: Under a sustained policy-easing regime (Singapore's transition toward living with COVID-19), incremental gains in TRANSIT mobility act as a leading indicator of relaxed movement restrictions, translating into higher RETAIL_REC within one week as commuters resume broader errand and leisure trips.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT mobility turned positive and stayed near 0.6-0.7 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a positive TRANSIT reading under the policy-easing regime.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PARKS mobility and decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility signals a behavioral substitution away from essential precautionary trips toward discretionary outdoor and recreational activity; this joint shift predicts a rise in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as discretionary spending patterns broaden.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM simultaneously declines week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -8.7 to -6.7 while GROCERY_PHARM fell from 43.1 to 42.9 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks despite concurrent PARKS increases and GROCERY_PHARM decreases.
